the following question: what are the implications of large capital inflows for the sustainability of current account deficits?

a new challenge for policymakers in emerging markets: that of resisting large current account deficits, or accepting them, depending on whether they are sustainable or not.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sustainability of a current account deficit is a function of the macroeconomic environment in which it occurs.
current account deficits that are not excessive are sustainable.
large current account deficits are unsustainable in the presence of a sharp increase in private spending, and in the presence of currency appreciation and a boom in the financial system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
current account deficits that are not excessive are sustainable in the long term.
large and excessive current account deficits should be a matter of public policy concern.
the current account is a good indicator of the health of the external balance, but it is not an indicator of the healthiness of the economy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sustainability of current account deficits is not a purely economic issue: it depends on the behaviour of the private sector and on the stance of monetary and fiscal policies.
large current account deficits can be excessive, but not necessarily so.

large current account deficits are not necessarily bad, but they can be a source of trouble if they are accompanied by unsustainable real exchange rate appreciations and excessive risk-taking in financial markets.
